# @ic-reactor/react

> The React bindings of ic-reactor 4: `ReactorProvider`, `useClient` and
> `useAuth`. Their guide is the one `@ic-reactor/core` ships.

Applies to `@ic-reactor/react` 4.0.0-beta.6.

Read `node_modules/@ic-reactor/core/llms.txt`. It is the one guide for both
packages: setup, the provider and `useAuth`, reads, writes, errors, values,
and a complete React example, with the rules each call enforces.

This package has no hook around `useQuery` or `useMutation`: call TanStack
Query's own hooks with the options the client builds,
`useQuery(client.queryOptions(...))` and
`useMutation(client.mutationOptions(...))`. It never re-exports
`@ic-reactor/core`: import each name from the package that defines it.

## Keys follow the caller a render shows

Call `useClient()` in the body of each component that builds keys or read
options, on every render, and build them from what it returns there, never from
a client held at module scope. It returns a view of the client for the caller
the render shows: one object per caller, a new one after a sign-in, a switch of
account or a sign-out, and the same one on every render while the caller stays.
List it in the dependencies of what is built from it (`useMemo(() =>
client.queryOptions(...), [client])`, an effect, a callback, as
`react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` asks); React Compiler memoizes on it the same
way, so what is memoized is built again for the new caller. Its `queryKey`,
`queryOptions`, `caller()` and `authState()` are that caller's, and its
`mutationOptions` send only as that caller: a write pressed before a switch
reaches the render is refused (`kind` `"cancelled"`, `code` `"caller_changed"`,
`mayHaveExecuted: false`) and sends nothing, so a click handler needs no check
of its own. Their `mutationKey` ends with that caller. A handler that awaits
`signIn()` and then calls `mutate` presses with the last committed render's
options, and is refused if the signed-in render has not committed yet (one that
suspends on the user's data): let the next render press, or make a direct call.
A canister's direct calls sign as the caller current when they run. Canisters,
`signIn`, `signOut` and the `QueryClient` are the client's own. It is never the
provider's client object: compare two clients by their `queryClient`.

Do not keep what it returns past the render: a view never moves on. Kept
anywhere else (`useState(client)`, `useRef(client)`, a `useMemo` or
`useCallback` with `[]`, a module variable), it stays the view of the caller
it was taken for: the component shows that caller's data, a read it starts
while someone else is signed in is cancelled, and a write through it is
refused. Nothing warns about it. A nested `ReactorProvider` given it holds
the client the view was made over. A component that calls `useClient()`
renders again on each sign-in, switch of account and sign-out, and never for
a change of status that leaves the caller as it is. On a server and while a
page hydrates the caller is anonymous, as for `useAuth()`, so the hydrating
render gets the anonymous caller's view: it finds what the server prefetched
and dehydrated, matches the server's HTML and sends nothing. Right after
hydrating, React renders the component again with the session's view, and
each read loads the user's keys once: until the user's data arrives, a read
shows its loading state, and a `useSuspenseQuery` read its boundary's
fallback. A tab whose caller is anonymous anyway (no session, or one that
expired or is signed in elsewhere) renders no `useClient()` component again,
and a client built with `identity` is always returned as it is.

A signed-in reload has three accepted costs:

- A Suspense boundary still dehydrated below a component that calls
  `useClient()` or `useAuth()` (its lazy code still loading, or its streamed
  HTML not arrived yet) is rendered on the client when that component
  moves on to the session: it shows its fallback, not the server's HTML, and
  React 18 reports a recoverable error. Its data is still the user's. A
  `useAuth()` component also moves on in a tab whose session expired or is
  signed in elsewhere. Render such a boundary where no component that renders with the caller sits above
  it, or pass it in as `children`, which a component's own update does not
  render again.
- A read the hydrating render built may still run once (a refetch of stale
  data on mount, or a fetch from an effect) and is then cancelled before
  anything is sent. A key that holds data keeps it as it was, and a fetch of
  it resolves with that data. A key with none fails, with `kind`
  `"cancelled"` and `code` `"caller_changed"`, until the anonymous caller is
  current again: the hydrating render's own reads never show it, but a
  listener of `client.queryClient.getQueryCache().subscribe()` (an
  `"updated"` event whose `action.type` is `"error"`; the client takes no
  `QueryCache` of yours), an effect that awaits the fetch and, for a
  `useSuspenseQuery` read the server rendered without dehydrating its data,
  React's `onRecoverableError` (as the reported error's `cause` on React 19)
  see it, so ignore `kind` `"cancelled"` there.
- Put a Suspense boundary above every component that reads with
  `useSuspenseQuery`, on React 18 and 19 alike. The move to the session is a
  synchronous update that such a read suspends until the user's data arrives:
  with a boundary above, it shows the fallback, then the user's data, and the
  rest of the page responds meanwhile. With none, React 18 refuses the update
  ("A component suspended while responding to synchronous input") and
  unmounts the root, so a signed-in reload renders nothing. React 19 keeps the
  server's HTML on screen, but until the user's data arrives, however long the
  read and its retries take, a click or any other update outside a transition
  commits nothing, and neither does a transition that renders the reading
  component again.
